bugs: No Idempotency-Key or other dedup token is sent to the partner. If the partner creates the shipment but the request hangs or times out client-side, the retry posts again and can create a duplicate shipment (app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:105). Verified with a probe.

failed() filters with `where('shipment_status', '!=', Sent)`. SQL NULL semantics mean an order whose shipment_status is NULL is never marked failed (app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:96). A probe confirmed it stays null. Only orders that skip markAsPaid can reach this state.
antipatterns: app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:37-40: RateLimited runs before WithoutOverlapping, so a job blocked by the overlap lock still uses up one of the 5 per-second slots.
app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:60-76: a chain of status-code ifs where $response->tooManyRequests() and similar helpers exist.
tests/Feature/SendOrderToWarehouseTest.php:159-161: hand-rolled Mockery Job mocks instead of withFakeQueueInteractions()/assertReleased().
tests/Feature/SendOrderToWarehouseTest.php:253: uses reflection to read the Backoff attribute, which tests configuration rather than behaviour.
strengths: markAsPaid uses an atomic conditional UPDATE (pending→paid) inside the transaction and dispatches afterCommit. Calling it twice, from stale instances, or on a cancelled order never dispatches a second job (verified by probe).
The job reloads with fresh(), checks trashed() and paid status, and runs under WithoutOverlapping per order plus a global RateLimited('warehouse') at Limit::perSecond(5).

On 429 the job releases with Retry-After clamped to 5–300s. 5xx and connection errors throw into backoff. MaxExceptions plus retryUntil keep retries bounded. HTTP timeouts are shorter than the job timeout.
A 422 calls fail() with the partner's message, so failed() records the reason and nothing is retried. failed() never downgrades a sent shipment and also works on trashed orders.
The exactly-once email uses an atomic claim on shipment_notified_at and rolls the claim back if sending throws.
Broad, well-named Pest tests: cancelled, unpaid, 422, 429 Retry-After cap/floor dataset, 5xx, hang, missing id, mail failure, failed() edge cases. Also adds .env.example entries.

bugs: markAsPaid has no guard. Calling it on an already shipped order sets shipment_status back to pending and dispatches again. The job then skips the request because a reference exists, so the order is stuck showing 'pending' even though it has a shipment reference (app/Models/Order.php:39-49). Verified by probe.

Calling markAsPaid twice dispatches two jobs, and calling it on a cancelled (soft-deleted) order still marks it paid and dispatches (app/Models/Order.php:41-48). Verified by probe. The job's trashed check stops the shipment itself, but checkout is not idempotent.

A 429 is thrown as a RequestException, so it ignores Retry-After, counts toward MaxExceptions(10) and enters generic backoff. A long rate-limit episode can use up the exception budget and mark the shipment failed (app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:97,116).

notifyCustomer sends first and then saves shipment_notified_at with no atomic claim. If the save or the worker fails after sending, the customer gets the email twice (app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:121-127).
antipatterns: app/Models/Order.php:15-23: shipment columns are mass-assignable through #[Fillable] even though the code writes them with forceFill.
app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:116: any 4xx except 408/429 counts as a permanent address rejection. A 401 from a bad token is recorded as a failed shipment with no retry.
app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:42: uses a fully-qualified \DateTimeInterface inline instead of an import.
tests/Feature/SendOrderToWarehouseTest.php: no test calls markAsPaid on an already paid or cancelled order, which hides the double-dispatch bug.
strengths: Sends an Idempotency-Key header, which guards against duplicate shipments when a hung request is retried.
Uses WithoutOverlapping per order before RateLimited (the better order) and a global Limit::perSecond(5).
failed() reloads with fresh() and skips orders that already have a shipment reference.
The 422 test goes end to end through markAsPaid on the sync queue. A rollback test checks that no job is pushed when the transaction fails.
Compact, readable job. preventStrayRequests is set globally in Pest.php.

bugs: markAsPaid is not atomic: it only checks the in-memory status. Two requests holding stale instances both dispatch a job (verified by probe: pushed 2 times), and nothing stops them running at the same time because there is no WithoutOverlapping. Both can POST, so only the Idempotency-Key header prevents a duplicate shipment (app/Models/Order.php:43, app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:33-36).
markAsPaid on a cancelled (soft-deleted) order still marks it paid and dispatches. The job refuses to ship, so this is harmless but noisy.
The 429 Retry-After value is not capped. A probe showed a release of 86400s, far beyond retryUntil(1h), so a single bad header ends the job by time-out (app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:137-141).
antipatterns: app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:23: DeleteWhenMissingModels does nothing useful here. Orders are only soft-deleted, so the model is never missing.
app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:51-55: nested if where `&& !` would read more simply.
app/Models/Order.php:15-24: all shipment and notification columns are mass-assignable, and the job writes them with update().
tests/Feature/OrderShipmentTest.php:108-117: fragile workaround (forgetInstance('mail.manager'), an event listener throwing, reading the array transport) to simulate a mail failure.
app/Models/Order.php:43: the idempotency check is inside the transaction but not locked, so the transaction gives a false impression of safety.
strengths: Sends an Idempotency-Key header, and a test names the hung-request duplicate scenario.

On 429 the job releases honouring Retry-After (default 30s). A 422 marks the shipment failed with the reason and completes cleanly without retrying or landing in failed_jobs. 5xx and timeouts throw into backoff, bounded by retryUntil and MaxExceptions.
The exactly-once email uses an atomic claim on shipment_notified_at with rollback on failure.
Modern test idioms: withFakeQueueInteractions()->assertReleased(delay:), Http::fakeSequence for recovery after a transient error, describe blocks, and an end-to-end sync-queue test.
Short job. The single comment explains a real constraint (releases count as attempts).

v.rationale:
All three suites pass: impl-1 25 tests, impl-2 22, impl-3 25. I ran throwaway probes against each implementation and then deleted them.

impl-1 ranks first. It is the most robust inside the app:
- markAsPaid uses an atomic conditional update, so it can't dispatch twice, even from stale instances or on a cancelled order.
- The job reloads the order, checks trashed() and paid status, and runs under a per-order WithoutOverlapping lock plus the global 5/s rate limit.
- On 429 it releases using Retry-After, clamped to 5–300s.
- A 422 goes through fail(), which records the reason. failed() never downgrades a sent shipment.
- The email is claimed atomically, so it is sent exactly once.
Its weak spots: it sends no idempotency key, so a request that hangs after the partner created the shipment can be retried into a duplicate. Its NULL-unsafe `!=` in failed() also misses orders with a null shipment_status, which only happens when markAsPaid is skipped.

impl-3 ranks second. It sends an Idempotency-Key, honours Retry-After and handles 422 cleanly, and its tests are the most modern (withFakeQueueInteractions, fakeSequence). But markAsPaid only checks the in-memory status. Probes showed two stale instances both dispatch, and with no overlap lock both jobs can POST. Retry-After is also uncapped (a probe got a release of 86400s).

impl-2 ranks third. A probe showed that markAsPaid on an already shipped order resets shipment_status to pending, and the order stays pending forever with a reference attached. It also dispatches on every call, including on cancelled orders. A 429 is treated as a generic exception that ignores Retry-After and uses up MaxExceptions. The email is sent before it is recorded, so a crash in between duplicates it. Its Idempotency-Key header and simple code don't make up for these bugs.
